Left the month off so this works whenever you send it. I added an exception path and a named owner on purpose: a freeze with no way through gets routed around by day two.

> **Code freeze from the 20th through the 27th.** Last merge to `main` is 6pm on the 20th. Normal merging resumes the morning of the 28th.
>
> **Still ships during the freeze:** sev1 and sev2 fixes, nothing else. Post the incident link in #eng-oncall, get a second reviewer, then merge.
>
> **Everything else waits.** Keep working and keep PRs open, just don't merge them. Get them reviewed before the 20th so the 28th isn't a pile-up of unreviewed branches.
>
> If you're not sure whether your change qualifies, ask me. I'd rather answer that twenty times than unpick a bad deploy on the 24th.

Wrote it assuming the fix is a stable idempotency key on the retry path. If it was actually a unique constraint or a processor-side change, the second paragraph is the only part that needs rewriting.

```
Fix duplicate charges on retried payments

Payment retries reused the request path but generated a fresh
idempotency key each attempt, so the processor treated every retry as a
new charge. Customers on a flaky connection could be charged two or
three times for one order.

Derive the idempotency key from the payment intent ID and the attempt
group instead of generating it per request, so all retries of the same
intent collapse to a single charge at the processor.

Add a regression test that retries one payment three times and asserts
exactly one charge is created.
```

Endpoint name, dates, and the v2 differences are mine, replace them. Removal date and migration path go in the first two lines because that is as far as most readers get.

> **`GET /v1/reports` will be removed on `[DATE]`.** Migrate to `GET /v2/reports` before then.
>
> **What happens and when**
>
> 1. **Now:** `/v1/reports` works exactly as it always has. Responses now carry `Deprecation: true` and `Sunset: [DATE]` headers so you can spot remaining callers in your logs.
> 2. **`[DATE MINUS 30 DAYS]`:** two scheduled brownouts of 30 minutes each, during which `/v1/reports` returns `410 Gone`. We'll announce each one a week ahead. These exist to surface traffic nobody remembers owning.
> 3. **`[DATE]`:** `/v1/reports` returns `410 Gone` permanently.
>
> **What changes in v2**
>
> - `report_id` is a string, not an integer
> - Pagination uses `cursor` instead of `page` and `per_page`
> - `created_at` is an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, not epoch seconds
> - Everything else keeps its name and shape
>
> Full field-by-field diff and a worked migration example: `[LINK]`
>
> If six months doesn't work for your team, reply here or write to `[EMAIL]` before `[DATE]` and tell us what you're blocked on. We'd rather hear about it now than during the first brownout.

First-day section only, so it stops at the first merged PR rather than covering the week. Repo names, tools, and channels are mine, swap in the real ones.

> ## Day one
>
> The goal today is narrow: your machine builds and runs the API, and you have one commit merged. Architecture, on-call, and the roadmap all wait until tomorrow. If you finish early, read code.
>
> 1. **Accounts and access.** Confirm you can sign in to Okta, GitHub, Slack, Linear, and the AWS dev account. IT provisioned these on `[DATE]`. Anything missing goes to #it-help right away, since access requests can take a day and everything below depends on them.
> 2. **Clone and build the API.** `git clone git@github.com:[ORG]/[REPO].git`, then follow `README.md`. A clean build takes about 15 minutes on a new laptop. If it fails, don't debug it alone, that's what step 6 is for.
> 3. **Run the test suite.** `make test`. It should pass fully on a fresh clone. If it doesn't, tell your buddy before you change anything, because a failing suite on `main` is our bug, not yours.
> 4. **Bring up the local stack.** `docker compose up`, then hit `http://localhost:8080/health` and confirm you get a `200`. This is the environment you'll spend most of your time in.
> 5. **Ship one commit.** Pick anything from the `good-first-issue` label in Linear, or fix a step in this document that was wrong. Open a PR, get a review, merge it. Doing this on day one means you never wonder whether the pipeline works.
> 6. **Meet your onboarding buddy.** `[NAME]` has a standing 30 minutes at `[TIME]` today. Bring whatever broke.
>
> Rule of thumb: if any step above eats more than 30 minutes, that's a bug in this document. Ping `[NAME]`, get unblocked, then fix the step for the next person.

Times, cause, and the fix are mine and need replacing before this goes out. I named the root cause plainly rather than saying "a technical issue," because vague incident notes generate more support tickets than they prevent.

> **Resolved: file uploads failed for 90 minutes on `[DATE]`, from 09:12 to 10:42 UTC.**
>
> During that window, most upload attempts failed with a `500` error. Uploads that returned a success response completed correctly. No stored files were lost, truncated, or corrupted, and no other part of the product was affected.
>
> **What happened.** A credential used by our storage service was rotated without the upload workers picking up the new value, so every request those workers made to storage was rejected. Our health checks monitored the API itself, which stayed up throughout, so we found out from customer reports rather than from an alert.
>
> **What we did.** Rolled back the credential change at 10:36 UTC and confirmed full recovery at 10:42 UTC.
>
> **What's changed since.** The upload path now has its own health check and pages on-call directly. Credential rotation now fails the deploy if any dependent service hasn't picked up the new value. Both landed on `[DATE]`.
>
> **If you were uploading during that window,** anything that failed is absent rather than partial, so a re-upload is safe and won't create duplicates. If you'd rather have us confirm what did land, write to `[EMAIL]` with your account ID and we'll check.
>
> Ninety minutes without uploads is a real cost to your day, and the alerting gap is the part we're least happy about. That one is fixed.

Two takes, they differ on how much they promise. A leans on confidentiality and is the safe pick if last year's follow-through was thin. B leads with what actually changed, which lifts response rates, but only send it if you can name a real change. I'd send B. Window and link are placeholders.

**A. Leads on confidentiality**

> This is our annual engineering satisfaction survey, and it's open until `[DATE]`. It takes about ten minutes. Responses go to `[TEAM/VENDOR]` and reach leadership only as aggregates, with free-text comments stripped of anything identifying, so answer as bluntly as you'd talk to a peer. Teams smaller than five are rolled up so nobody's answers can be traced back. We ask the same questions every year on purpose: the year-over-year movement is the part that tells us something.

**B. Leads on what changed**

> Last year's survey said interviews were eating too much of your week and that the on-call rotation was too thin. We cut the interview load per engineer roughly in half and added two people to the rotation. Neither is finished, and neither would have happened without the survey saying it plainly. This year's survey is open until `[DATE]` and takes about ten minutes. Responses go to `[TEAM/VENDOR]` and reach leadership only as aggregates, with free-text stripped of identifying details. Tell us the thing you'd tell a peer, not the thing you'd tell a manager. `[LINK]`

Version, date, and links are mine. I put the removal above the feature: people who used the export button need to see it first, and nobody scrolls release notes.

```
## v2.4.0 - [DATE]

### Removed

- **The legacy export button is gone.** The "Export (legacy)" control in
  the reports toolbar has been removed. Use **Export > CSV** or
  **Export > JSON** in the same toolbar instead. Both produce the same
  columns as the legacy export plus `updated_at`. Scheduled exports that
  were created with the legacy button keep running unchanged, so there is
  nothing to migrate there. Anything scripted against
  `/reports/export/legacy` needs to move to `/reports/export` before
  `[DATE]`, when that route starts returning `410 Gone`.

### Added

- **Single sign-on via SAML 2.0.** Available on `[PLAN]` and above.
  Workspace owners can configure an identity provider under
  **Settings > Security > SSO**. Tested against Okta, Entra ID, and
  Google Workspace; any SAML 2.0 provider should work. Just-in-time
  provisioning is on by default, so a user who authenticates
  successfully gets an account with the default role. Enforcing SSO for
  a workspace is a separate toggle and is off until you turn it on, so
  enabling SSO will not lock anyone out mid-session. Setup guide:
  `[LINK]`
```

Firm without being hostile, since you still need these people to help you. It names a date, a business cost, and one specific next step, which is the floor for an escalation that actually moves. Ticket numbers, names, and dates are mine.

**Subject:** `[VENDOR] integration blocked 3 weeks, ticket [NUMBER] has no owner`

> Hi `[NAME]`,
>
> I'm escalating because our `[VENDOR]` integration has been blocked for three weeks and support ticket `[NUMBER]` hasn't had a substantive reply in nine days.
>
> **Where things stand.** Since `[DATE]`, calls to `[ENDPOINT]` in the sandbox return `[ERROR]` for our account, while the same request against `[OTHER ENDPOINT]` succeeds. We've confirmed the credentials, the account scopes, and the request signing on our side, and we sent full request and response logs with the original ticket on `[DATE]`. We've had two automated status updates since and no engineer response.
>
> **What this is costing.** The integration is the last item before our `[DATE]` launch. We're now `[N]` weeks from that date with roughly `[N]` days of work left once we're unblocked, so the date goes if this doesn't move this week.
>
> **What I'm asking for.** One engineer assigned to ticket `[NUMBER]` with a reply by `[DATE]`, even if the reply is "we can't reproduce it, send us X." I'd also take 30 minutes on a call with someone who works on `[ENDPOINT]` directly, and I'll bring the logs and a reproducible request. I'm free `[DAYS/TIMES]`.
>
> If this belongs with someone else on your side, tell me who and I'll take it there.
>
> `[YOUR NAME]`
> `[TITLE]`, `[COMPANY]`
> `[PHONE]`
